sections.markdown:
## C — Name and address changes, military and license designations, driving records, legal presence and the Arizona road test
Knowledge domain: the customer-service rules every Arizona applicant meets before and after licensing — reporting name and address changes, how discharged military personnel and designation holders are treated, how to get a driving record, the federal legal-presence requirement, and what the road test and the test vehicle must look like.

FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A01
If MVD revokes, suspends or cancels your license, you may owe a fresh application fee in addition to a reinstatement fee. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A01
MVD lists an abandoned vehicle fee of $500 ($600 when the vehicle is left on federal land) and a $25 fee for a returned check. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A01
To save time, check AZMVDNow.gov first to see whether your transaction can be finished online, and use it to fill out an application for an ID, driver license or title. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A01
AZMVDNow.gov is also where you book an appointment for a road test, a Travel credential or a license renewal. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A01
Offices are busiest on the first two and last two days of each month and on the day after a holiday, and most offices stay closed until noon on the second Wednesday of every month. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A01
Bring your out-of-state driver license to MVD, because it serves as a secondary form of identification and can waive the written or road test. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A01
When visiting MVD, bring your required identification, any out-of-state title, registration and license plates, and have the vehicle identification number (VIN) ready. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A01
Besides cash, most MVD fees can be paid by credit card, cashier's check or money order, and checks or money orders should be made out to Motor Vehicle Division. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A01
Arizona law requires you to tell MVD about any change of name or address within 10 days. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A01
If you skip reporting a change, renewal notices and other mail about your license or vehicles may never reach you, and police may cite you. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F11 | anchor: A01
An address change can be filed online at AZMVDNow.gov by giving your full name, the new address with zip code, your license number and birth date, plus the final four digits of your Social Security number. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F12 | anchor: A01
Reporting a new address does not reprint your card; to show the new address on the credential you must apply for and buy a replacement license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F13 | anchor: A02
Because MVD links all of your records, one address change updates your license or ID record and every vehicle record that lists you as first registered owner. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F14 | anchor: A02
A name change is done in person at any MVD office or at an authorized third party office that handles driver licenses, with identification in both your new and your former name. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F15 | anchor: A02
To have the new name printed on your license you apply for a replacement license, and every name must be verifiable against Social Security Administration records. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F16 | anchor: A02
Service members based in Arizona are not counted as Arizona residents when they qualify for the Soldiers and Sailors Relief Act exemption. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F17 | anchor: A02
After discharge, a former service member may work in Arizona for up to 90 days without an Arizona license, but only if all of the listed conditions are met. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F18 | anchor: A02
Those conditions are a valid license from another state or country, driving a vehicle that needs only a Class D license, and working for an organization that operates both in Arizona and in at least one other state or country. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F19 | anchor: A02
A Veteran Designation, printed as the word VETERAN on the front of the license, instruction permit or ID, is available to United States military veterans and active duty service members. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F20 | anchor: A02
A Native American Designation, printed as NATIVE AMERICAN on the front of the credential, is available to enrolled members of a federally recognized tribe located in Arizona. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F21 | anchor: A02
Adding either designation requires a new application and a new photo, and the standard transaction fees apply. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F22 | anchor: A03
A copy of your driving or motor vehicle record is available through AZMVDNow.gov, or by filling out the Motor Vehicle Record Request form 46-4416 and taking it to an MVD or Authorized Third Party office, where you must show identification. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F23 | anchor: A03
Under Arizona Revised Statutes section 28-3153(D), MVD may not issue or renew a driver license or ID card unless the applicant proves that federal law authorizes their presence in the United States. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F24 | anchor: A03
MVD warns that identification requirements can change without notice. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F25 | anchor: A03
Road test appointments are booked at AZMVDNow.gov, booking ahead is strongly encouraged so you can test when you arrive, and checking several offices helps you find the earliest slot. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F26 | anchor: A03
When a road test is required, an examiner rides in your vehicle, directs you along a route with varied traffic situations, and grades both specific actions and your overall ability to drive safely. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F27 | anchor: A03
Extreme weather or unsafe conditions can lead MVD to suspend road testing. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F28 | anchor: A03
Before the road test you must show that you understand Arizona traffic signs. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F29 | anchor: A03
You must also respond to spoken English directions: stop, slow down, change lanes left or right, drive straight ahead, turn at the next street, corner, stop sign or light, confirm your speedometer works, and fasten your seat belt. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F30 | anchor: A03
You supply the road test vehicle, and it must have working brakes, brake lights, turn signals and horn, an uncracked windshield, inside and outside rearview mirrors, and tires in good condition. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

Misconceptions: filing an address change does not update the printed card — a replacement license is needed for that; an out-of-state license is not ignored at MVD, it can serve as secondary identification and may waive testing; the examiner does not provide a car, the applicant brings a safe one.
Mnemonics: Ten days, tell MVD — name or address; for a discharged service member to work here on an outside license, think License, Light vehicle, Linked employer.
Glossary: VIN means the vehicle identification number; AZMVDNow.gov is the official MVD online service site; Authorized Third Party means a private office licensed by MVD to perform its services; legal presence means proof that federal law authorizes you to be in the United States.
Dynamic facts: fees, office closure days, online service lists and identification requirements are service details the manual itself says may change, so confirm them on azdot.gov or AZMVDNow.gov before relying on them.
